CA.name: California: a PG&E home on time-of-use rate E-TOU-C
CA.note: Bundled service (PG&E buys the power), Income Tier 3 (no CARE or FERA discount), basic (not all-electric) baseline quantities. PG&E's service area is in CAISO; the wholesale reference is CAISO's main hub in the warehouse, SP15, while most PG&E homes sit in the NP15 zone.

totals.name: Energy charge (total rate)
totals.what: The price per kWh for each hour, higher from 4 to 9 p.m.
totals.why: Power costs more in the evening, when solar fades and demand is still high, so the rate asks homes to shift use.
totals.quote: E-TOU-C TOTAL BUNDLED RATES Total Energy Rates ($ per kWh) PEAK OFF-PEAK Summer Total Usage $0.52240 (R) $0.39940 (R) Baseline Credit (Applied to Baseline Usage Only) ($0.08140) (I) ($0.08140) (I) Winter Total Usage $0.39757 (R) $0.36757 (R)

tou_rule.quote: TOU period usage is assigned to tiers on a pro-rated basis. For example, if twenty percent of a customer's usage is in the peak period, then twenty percent of the total usage in each tier will be treated as on-peak usage.

periods.quote: Peak: 4:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. All days

baseline_credit.name: Baseline credit
baseline_credit.what: A credit per kWh on the first block of use each day, the baseline allowance.
baseline_credit.why: California law gives every home a basic amount of power at a lower price; use above it pays more.
baseline_credit.quote: Baseline Credit (Applied to Baseline Usage Only) ($0.08140) (I) ($0.08140) (I)

baseline_quantities.unit: kWh per day, [summer, winter], Code B (basic) quantities

base_services.quote: Base Services Charge Rates ($ per customer per day) Income Tier 1 $0.19713 (N) Income Tier 2 $0.39688 (N) Income Tier 3 $0.79343 (N)
base_services.what: A fixed charge per day, set by household income.
base_services.why: Part of the cost of the grid does not change with use; a daily charge collects it and lowers the per-kWh rates (the tariff says the charge's revenue reduces the energy rates).
base_services.components_quote: Distribution Income Tier 1 ($0.10751) (N) Income Tier 2 ($0.02710) (N) Income Tier 3 $0.36945 (N) Public Purpose Program Income Tier 1 $0.19131 (N) Income Tier 2 $0.31065 (N) Income Tier 3 $0.31065 (N)

climate_credit.name: California Climate Credit
climate_credit.what: A credit on the bill, twice a year, per household.
climate_credit.why: California returns part of the money power plants pay for their carbon emissions to households.
climate_credit.quote: California Climate Credit (per household, semi-annual payment occurring in the August and September bill cycles) ($36.18) (N)

components.name: Generation
components.what: The power itself: what PG&E pays to generate or buy electricity.
components.why: Someone has to make the electricity; this is its cost.

components.name: Bundled Power Charge Indifference Adjustment
components.what: An adjustment for the cost of older power contracts, shown with generation on the bill.
components.why: Contracts signed years ago for all customers are shared fairly between customers who stayed and those who left for another supplier.
components.quote: Bundled Power Charge Indifference Adjustment (all usage)*** ($0.01011)

components.name: Distribution
components.what: The local wires, poles and transformers that bring power to the home.
components.why: The neighborhood grid has to be built, maintained and repaired; this pays for it.

components.name: New System Generation Charge
components.what: A charge for new power plants built for reliability, shown with distribution on the bill.
components.why: The state asks utilities to build or contract new capacity so there is enough power on the hottest days.

components.name: Conservation Incentive Adjustment
components.what: A credit on use within the baseline and a charge on use above it.
components.why: It is how the baseline credit is built: use above the baseline allowance pays more.
components.quote: Conservation Incentive Adjustment (Baseline Usage) ($0.02786) (I) Conservation Incentive Adjustment (Over Baseline Usage) $0.05354 (R)

components.name: Transmission
components.what: The high-voltage lines that carry power from plants to cities.
components.why: Long-distance lines are shared across the state's grid and paid for by all its users.

components.name: Transmission Rate Adjustments
components.what: Adjustments to the transmission charge, shown with transmission on the bill.
components.why: Transmission costs are trued up to what was actually spent.

components.name: Reliability Services
components.what: A small charge for services that keep the grid stable, shown with transmission.
components.why: The grid operator buys services that keep voltage and frequency steady.

components.name: Public Purpose Programs
components.what: State programs: energy efficiency, help for low-income customers, research.
components.why: California funds these programs through every bill.

components.name: Nuclear Decommissioning
components.what: Money set aside to take apart retired nuclear plants safely.
components.why: Nuclear plants must be dismantled and cleaned up after they close.

components.name: Competition Transition Charges
components.what: A charge left from the move to competitive power markets in the late 1990s.
components.why: Some older costs are still being paid off.

components.name: Energy Cost Recovery Amount
components.what: A small charge that recovers past energy costs.
components.why: Past costs approved by the regulator are paid off over time.

components.name: Wildfire Fund Charge
components.what: A charge for California's fund that pays wildfire damage claims against utilities.
components.why: Wildfires started by power lines cause great damage; the state fund pays claims so utilities stay solvent.

components.name: Wildfire Hardening Charge
components.what: A charge for work that makes the grid less likely to start fires.
components.why: Covering lines, clearing trees and undergrounding cut fire risk.

components.name: Recovery Bond Charge
components.what: A charge that repays bonds the utility issued.
components.why: Some large costs are financed with bonds and repaid over many years.

components.name: Recovery Bond Credit
components.what: A credit that offsets the recovery bond charge.
components.why: The bond charge is offset for bundled customers, so the two cancel.

presentation.quote: Transmission, Transmission Rate Adjustments and Reliability Service charges are combined for presentation on customer bills. ** Distribution and New System Generation Charges are combined for presentation on customer bills.

labels.peak_share: 20 percent in peak hours, the tariff's own example (Sheet 1)

TX.name: Texas: a home in Oncor's area of ERCOT
TX.note: In most of ERCOT, a retail electric provider sells the power and a wires company (here Oncor) delivers it. The retailer's energy charge is set by the plan the customer picks: it is an input. Oncor's delivery charges are passed through by the retailer.

energy_default.derivation: EIA's average Texas residential price for July 2026 (158.8 USD/MWh, all customers of all utilities and retailers) less Oncor's delivery charges at 600 kWh, so the default bill at 600 kWh matches that average; an assumption: enter the energy charge on your plan's Electricity Facts Label
energy_default.arithmetic: 0.1588 - 0.061322 (Oncor per kWh) - 4.06 / 600 (Oncor fixed per kWh at 600) = 0.090711, rounded to 0.0907

fixed.name: Customer Charge
fixed.what: A fixed monthly charge per customer for Oncor's account costs.
fixed.why: Billing and customer service cost the same whether a home uses a little or a lot.
fixed.quote: MONTHLY RATE I. Base Rate Charges: Customer Charge $ 1.48 per Retail Customer Metering Charge $ 2.58 per Retail Customer Distribution System Charge $ 0.036043 per kWh

fixed.name: Metering Charge
fixed.what: A fixed monthly charge for the meter and reading it.
fixed.why: Every home has a meter to install, read and maintain.

per_kwh.name: Distribution System Charge
per_kwh.what: Oncor's charge per kWh for the local wires and poles.
per_kwh.why: The neighborhood grid has to be built and kept up.

per_kwh.name: Transmission Cost Recovery Factor (TCRF)
per_kwh.what: A charge for the high-voltage transmission lines across ERCOT.
per_kwh.why: Every wires company in ERCOT pays for the shared transmission grid; it passes the cost through.
per_kwh.quote: Effective Date ($/kWh) ($/kWh) ($/NCP kW) ($/4CP kW) ($/kWh) ($/NCP kW) ($/4CP kW) ($/4CP kW) ($/4CP kW) August 1, 2026 0.019046
per_kwh.effective: 2026-08-01 (Rider TCRF, 6.1.1.6.1; the first column is Residential Service)

per_kwh.name: Energy Efficiency Cost Recovery Factor (EECRF)
per_kwh.what: A charge for Oncor's energy efficiency programs.
per_kwh.why: Texas law requires wires companies to fund programs that cut waste.
per_kwh.effective: 2026-03-01 (Rider EECRF, 6.1.1.6.3; the first column is Residential Service)

per_kwh.name: Distribution Cost Recovery Factor (DCRF)
per_kwh.what: A charge for new distribution investment between rate cases; now zero.
per_kwh.why: It recovers new wires spending until the next full rate review, which reset it.
per_kwh.effective: 2026-06-01 (Rider DCRF, 6.1.1.6.4; the first column is Residential Service)

per_kwh.name: Nuclear Decommissioning Charge (NDC)
per_kwh.what: A charge to take apart retired nuclear plants; now zero for homes.
per_kwh.why: Nuclear plants must be dismantled safely after they close.
per_kwh.quote: Nuclear Decommissioning Rate Schedule Charge Factor (NDCF) Res idential Service $ 0.000000 per kWh

per_kwh.name: Rate Case Expense Surcharge (RCE)
per_kwh.what: A temporary charge for the cost of Oncor's last rate review.
per_kwh.why: The regulator lets the utility recover the approved cost of the case, about a year.
per_kwh.effective: Rider RCE (6.1.1.6.5), Docket No. 58306, in effect until $8,291,399 has been billed

per_kwh.name: Mobile Generation Rider (MG)
per_kwh.what: A charge for portable generators Oncor uses to restore power after storms.
per_kwh.why: Texas lets wires companies lease mobile generation for outages.
per_kwh.effective: 2025-12-01 (Rider MG, 6.1.1.6.6; the first column is Residential Service)

per_kwh.name: Interim Surcharge (IS)
per_kwh.what: A temporary charge that makes up the difference between old and new rates for part of 2026.
per_kwh.why: The new rates approved in 2026 apply from January 1, 2026; this collects the gap.
per_kwh.quote: Rate Schedule IS Residential Service $ 0.003633 per kWh
per_kwh.effective: Rider IS (6.1.1.6.7), in effect through December 2026
